question.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}3x\,\text{d}V
$$

where $R$ is the type III region given by 

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le x,\,0\le z\le 2-x\}.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}3x\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}{\int }_{0}^{x}3x\,dy\,dz\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}{\int }_{0}^{x}3x\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}[{\int }_{0}^{x}3x\,dy]dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}3x[y]_{y=0}^{y=x}dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}3x(x-0)\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}3{x}^{2}\,dz\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x}3{x}^{2}\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{2-x}\,\text{d}z]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{2}{[z]}_{z=0}^{z=2-x}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{2}(2-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(6{x}^{2}-3{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}(6{x}^{2}-3{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & ={[2{x}^{3}-\frac{3}{4}{x}^{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =(16-12)-0 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
